Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Split like a Wamsoft game**: kagex-release's Windows, Linux, Steam and macOS builds always ship `data.xp3` (start-up script, framework, main scripts) with an archive per media folder beside it (`bgimage.xp3`, `fgimage.xp3`, `voice.xp3`, `bgm.xp3`, `scenario.xp3`, `video.xp3`...), encrypted and signed or not. The *Split large archives* option is gone. The web, Android and iOS builds keep one `data.xp3`
- **Hidden names stay in `data.xp3`**: with *Hide names*, every file in `data.xp3` and the media archives is stored under a hashed name, except `data.xp3`'s `startup.tjs`, which opens the rest. No `data.xpc` and no `data/` folder any more. It works with signing too
- A game with its own `data/system` needs this release's framework for hidden names, and for split archives on macOS (the check says so)
- kagex-release 0.9.2 downloads the 0.9.2 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.9.2/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
